title: ESUS / cryptogenic stroke: antithrombotic and PFO
keyNumbers: Age 18–60, nonlacunar stroke of undetermined cause, PFO with high-risk anatomic features: PFO closure + long-term antiplatelet over antiplatelet alone
Age 18–60, PFO without high-risk features: Benefit of closure not well established
question: What antithrombotic and workup decisions follow stroke of undetermined source?
population: Nonlacunar stroke without a cause after standard workup (ESUS / cryptogenic)

rules.condition: No AF or other anticoagulation indication found
rules.recommendation: Antiplatelet therapy, not empiric anticoagulation (NAVIGATE ESUS and RESPECT ESUS showed no DOAC benefit)
evidenceNote: Kleindorfer 2021 and AHA 2026: COR 1, LOE A (antiplatelet over OAC in noncardioembolic stroke)

rules.condition: Minor stroke or high-risk TIA within the DAPT window
Cryptogenic stroke without contraindication to anticoagulation
rules.recommendation: Long-term rhythm monitoring (mobile outpatient telemetry, implantable loop recorder) to find intermittent AF

rules.condition: ESUS — looking for cardioaortic source or shunt
rules.recommendation: TEE, cardiac CT or cardiac MRI might be reasonable

rules.condition: Age 18–60, nonlacunar stroke of undetermined cause, PFO with high-risk anatomic features
rules.recommendation: PFO closure + long-term antiplatelet over antiplatelet alone
Benefit of closure not well established
Switch to oral anticoagulation — see af-stroke-anticoag-timing
evidenceNote: Kleindorfer 2021: COR 1, LOE A (OAC with AF)

institutionVaries: Loop-recorder referral pathway and PFO-closure heart team
pearls: High-risk PFO features vary by trial (larger shunt, atrial septal aneurysm) — RoPE/PASCAL not in the stored sources
Serious periprocedural complications of closure ~4.9% at ≤60 y vs 10.9% older (claims data, Kleindorfer)

ARCADIA (cryptogenic stroke, age ≥45, no AF, atrial cardiopathy = PTFV1 >5000 μV·ms, NT-proBNP >250 pg/mL or LA diameter index ≥3 cm/m²; apixaban vs aspirin 81 mg, n=1015): recurrent stroke 4.4%/yr in both arms (HR 1.00); stopped for futility; no greater benefit at higher biomarker levels
sources: Kleindorfer DO, et al. 2021 Guideline for the Prevention of Stroke in Patients With Stroke and Transient Ischemic Attack (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2021;52:e364-e467. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000375
Prabhakaran S, et al. 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2026;57:e316-e436. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000513

Kamel H, et al. Apixaban to Prevent Recurrence After Cryptogenic Stroke in Patients With Atrial Cardiopathy: The ARCADIA Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2024;331(7):573-581. doi:10.1001/jama.2023.27188
